summary: Wenatchee NF summit in Chelan County, WA; a 1914 camp lookout, a 1925 D-6 cabin, an 18-ft L-4 tower (1948) gone by 1967; footings still visible per captions.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin (finished 1925), replaced in 1948 by an 18-foot tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1967 per the FFLOS register (FireLookout.com says destroyed). Willhite's photo captions show footings still in place.

access.note: Ruby Creek FS Road 7404 from Highway 97, then an old road bed under a mile to the summit; no closure appears in these sources

visit.trail_note: Follow Ruby Creek FS Road 7404 to its end, then the old road bed (under a mile). A road near the top can be walked for the last stretch.

events.note: Camp lookout developed; one of four original sites testing heliograph signaling
Forest Service building a telephone line from the lookout to the Leavenworth forest office
D-6 cupola cabin finished (FireLookout.com dates it to 1924)
Pilot spotted fires on Polollie Ridge and Waptus Lake and dropped a note at the lookout; reports phoned to a ranger and crews sent in
Cupola cabin replaced by an 18-foot tower with an L-4 cab
Tower removed per the FFLOS register; FireLookout.com says destroyed; Willhite says it lasted until 1967

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS register and Willhite give 1925 (Willhite says the cabin was finished that year, after construction began in 1924). FireLookout.com gives 1924 as the build year. The story uses 1925 and notes the difference.
The FFLOS register says the tower was removed in 1967; FireLookout.com says destroyed; Willhite says it lasted until 1967. The story reports the removal and notes FireLookout.com's wording.
FireLookout.com names Leonard Webb for 1950; Willhite names Mr. and Mrs. Don Fife. The story gives both without choosing between them.

notes_for_editor: Three sources. The FFLOS and FireLookout.com lists are in close agreement; Willhite's long history is a single hobbyist's compilation of newspaper clips, which we did not check against the originals. Lookout names differ in 1932-1935 across sources (Harold Kester, H.B. Kester, Albert Kester), so no staffing list is written beyond the lines quoted. Willhite's photo captions for the footings, garbage pit and toilet hole are undated, so the story attributes 'still in place' to the captions without giving a date. The brief's 'gone' status is consistent with the sources. The Weebly page (washingtonlookouts.weebly.com/tiptop.html) was read but not used. Check for a current Forest Service road status on Road 7404 before publishing the access level.
